Nenhuma métrica chega sozinha. Com class: No single metric is enough. With very unbalanced classes, accuracy is misleading: look at recall, F1 and the confusion matrix. In regression, compare the error with the scale of the target.
Num teste com 95 alunos que passam e 5 q: In a test with 95 students who pass and 5 who fail, a model that always answers “pass” has 95% accuracy and finds no student at risk (0% recall for that class).

A accuracy não chega: um palpite fixo já: Accuracy is not enough: a fixed guess would already give 96%. You need to look at recall and F1.
Quando uma classe domina, acertar muito: When one class dominates, getting a high score is easy. The per-class metrics show whether the model also finds the rare class.
Generalizar é funcionar bem em dados nov: Generalising means working well on new data, not only on the data used for training.
Um modelo que decora o treino tem notas: A model that memorises the training data scores high there and poorly in real life (overfitting). A model that is too simple fails everywhere (underfitting).
Comparam-se as notas do treino e do test: The training and test scores (and the cross-validation score) are compared. The gap between them and the distance to the simple baseline give hints about what is going on.
Treino muito acima do teste: sobreajuste: Training far above test: overfitting. Training and test both weak: underfitting. Close scores above the baseline: a good sign. With little data none of this is conclusive.
Uma árvore de decisão sem limite de prof: A decision tree with no depth limit can have an F1 of 100% on training and 70% on test: it learned the noise in the training data.
O R² é 0,98 no treino e 0,55 no teste. Q: R² is 0.98 on training and 0.55 on test. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A grande queda do treino para o teste in: The large drop from training to test shows the model memorised the training data and does not generalise.
Treinar vários algoritmos nos mesmos dad: Training several algorithms on the same data, with the same split and the same validation, to compare them fairly.
Nenhum algoritmo é o melhor em tudo. Só: No algorithm is the best at everything. Only by comparing do you find out which one suits your data.
Todos usam o mesmo treino e o mesmo test: They all use the same training and test sets. The choice of the best uses cross-validation on the training data only; the test set is kept for the final score.
Critérios diferentes podem eleger modelo: Different criteria can pick different models (for example, F1 and recall). If the difference is smaller than the cross-validation deviation, the models are equivalent: prefer the simpler and faster one.
Uma floresta aleatória pode ganhar por 0: A random forest may beat a logistic regression by 0.5 F1 points but train 50 times slower. In that case the difference is rarely worth it.

Vejo-os como equivalentes e escolho o ma: I see them as equivalent and pick the simpler or faster one.
A diferença (0,02) é menor do que o desv: The difference (0.02) is smaller than the deviation (0.04 to 0.05): it is within the noise.
Os hiperparâmetros são as definições do: Hyperparameters are the algorithm settings you choose before training (depth, number of trees, C...). Optimising means searching for the best values.
Os valores por omissão servem, mas raram: The default values work, but they are rarely the best for your data.
A procura em grelha (GridSearchCV) testa: Grid search (GridSearchCV) tests every combination. Random search (RandomizedSearchCV) tests some at random, and is faster. Both use cross-validation on the training data only.
O teste só é usado no fim, uma vez, para: The test set is only used at the end, once, to compare before and after. If the model improves in cross-validation but not on the test set, the search over-adjusted to the validation folds.
Numa floresta aleatória, testar 3 valore: In a random forest, testing 3 values of n_estimators and 3 of max_depth gives 9 combinations. With 3 validation folds, that is 27 training runs.
Porque é que NÃO se escolhem hiperparâme: Why do we NOT choose hyperparameters by looking at the test set?
Porque o teste deixa de ser «dados novos: Because the test set stops being “new data” and the final score becomes optimistic.
Because the test set is too small.
Se o teste decide, o modelo acaba por se: If the test set decides, the model ends up adjusting to it and we no longer have an honest score.
